concepts.name: Position, displacement and distance
concepts.summary: Distinguish position, displacement and distance travelled and describe motion along a line with a coordinate axis.

concepts.name: Speed and velocity
concepts.summary: Explain velocity as the rate of change of position with direction and compute average speed and velocity.

concepts.name: Acceleration as rate of change
concepts.summary: Explain acceleration as the rate of change of velocity and interpret its sign relative to motion.

concepts.name: Force as push or pull
concepts.summary: Describe forces as vector interactions and identify common ones such as weight, normal force, friction and tension.

concepts.name: Newton's three laws
concepts.summary: State and explain inertia, F=ma and action-reaction pairs in everyday situations.

concepts.name: Free fall near Earth
concepts.summary: Explain that all objects fall with the same acceleration g of about 9.8 m/s² when air resistance is negligible.

concepts.name: Mass versus weight
concepts.summary: Distinguish mass as amount of inertia from weight as gravitational force W=mg.

misconceptions.text: A moving object needs a continuing net force to keep moving at constant velocity.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones in the absence of air resistance.
Negative acceleration always means the object is slowing down.

concepts.name: Constant-acceleration kinematic equations
concepts.summary: Select and apply the equations relating displacement, velocity, acceleration and time to one-dimensional problems.

concepts.name: Motion graphs
concepts.summary: Read slopes and areas of position, velocity and acceleration graphs to find velocity, acceleration and displacement.

concepts.name: Vector components and resolution
concepts.summary: Resolve forces and velocities into perpendicular components using trigonometry and recombine them.

concepts.name: Projectile motion
concepts.summary: Treat horizontal and vertical motion independently to find range, flight time and maximum height.

concepts.name: Free-body diagrams
concepts.summary: Draw all forces acting on a single body and write Newton's second law along chosen axes.

concepts.name: Friction and inclined planes
concepts.summary: Apply friction coefficients and weight components to find acceleration on level and inclined surfaces.

concepts.name: Work and kinetic energy
concepts.summary: Compute work as force times displacement along the force and kinetic energy as ½mv².

misconceptions.text: A projectile at its peak has zero acceleration.
Friction always opposes the motion of an object, even when it is what accelerates it, such as a car's wheels or a box on a belt.
The normal force always equals the weight of the object.

concepts.name: Work-energy theorem
aliases: net work equals change in kinetic energy
concepts.summary: Use net work equals change in kinetic energy to solve speed and distance problems without time.

concepts.name: Conservative forces and potential energy
concepts.summary: Define potential energy for conservative forces and apply conservation of mechanical energy, accounting for non-conservative work.

concepts.name: Power
concepts.summary: Compute power as rate of energy transfer, including P=Fv.

concepts.name: Momentum and impulse
concepts.summary: Relate impulse, force over time, to change in momentum.

concepts.name: Conservation of linear momentum
concepts.summary: Identify when a system is isolated in a direction and use momentum conservation to analyse interactions.

concepts.name: Elastic and inelastic collisions
concepts.summary: Classify collisions by kinetic energy conservation and solve one- and two-dimensional cases.

concepts.name: Simple harmonic motion of springs
concepts.summary: Apply Hooke's law and find period, frequency and energy of a mass on a spring.

concepts.name: Uniform circular motion
concepts.summary: Explain that circular motion requires a net inward force and compute v²/r and the required force.

misconceptions.text: Kinetic energy is conserved in all collisions.
Centrifugal force is a real outward force acting on an object in circular motion.
The period of a mass on a spring depends on the amplitude of oscillation.

concepts.name: Rotational kinematics and dynamics
concepts.summary: Map linear quantities onto angular ones and relate angular acceleration to net torque.

concepts.name: Torque and static equilibrium
concepts.summary: Compute torque as r×F and apply zero net force and torque conditions to structures.

concepts.name: Moment of inertia
concepts.summary: Analyse how mass distribution and axis choice determine rotational inertia, using standard shapes and the parallel-axis theorem.

concepts.name: Angular momentum conservation
concepts.summary: Apply conservation of angular momentum when net external torque is zero, as in a spinning skater.

concepts.name: Rolling motion and energy
concepts.summary: Combine translational and rotational kinetic energy to analyse rolling bodies on inclines.

concepts.name: Newtonian gravitation and orbits
concepts.summary: Use the inverse-square law to derive circular orbital speed and period and apply Kepler's laws.

concepts.name: Gravitational potential energy and escape
concepts.summary: Evaluate orbital energies and escape speed using the potential -GMm/r.

concepts.name: Pendulum and damped oscillations
concepts.summary: Judge when the simple pendulum is harmonic and analyse damping, driving and resonance.

misconceptions.text: Astronauts in orbit float because there is no gravity there.
A heavier object always has a larger moment of inertia regardless of how its mass is distributed or about which axis.
The pendulum period depends on the bob's mass and is independent of the length.

concepts.name: Lagrangian formulation
concepts.summary: Derive equations of motion from L=T-V with generalised coordinates and judge when this beats Newtonian force analysis.

concepts.name: Symmetries and conservation laws
concepts.summary: Link translation, rotation and time invariance to conservation of momentum, angular momentum and energy.

concepts.name: Central-force problem
concepts.summary: Reduce the two-body problem to an effective one-dimensional potential and classify orbits by energy and angular momentum.

concepts.name: Rigid body rotation in 3D
concepts.summary: Use the inertia tensor and principal axes to explain torque-free rotation, precession and gyroscopic effects.

concepts.name: Non-inertial reference frames
concepts.summary: Formulate dynamics in accelerating and rotating frames and evaluate centrifugal and Coriolis effects.

concepts.name: Small oscillations and normal modes
concepts.summary: Linearise about equilibrium and construct normal modes of coupled systems.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian mechanics and phase space
concepts.summary: Use Hamilton's equations and phase-space portraits to analyse dynamics and stability.

concepts.name: Limits of Newtonian models
concepts.summary: Evaluate where classical models fail or lose predictability, including chaos and relativistic or quantum regimes.

misconceptions.text: The Lagrangian approach gives different physics from Newton's laws rather than an equivalent reformulation.
Fictitious forces like Coriolis are not real, so they can be ignored when analysing motion in a rotating frame.
Deterministic equations of motion always allow long-term prediction.
